rounds.text: Nitta Gelatin India Ltd trades at an attractive P/E of 12.1x, which sits well below its sector benchmark of 20.27x [E1, E6]. Fundamental quality is exceptional, highlighted by an impressive ROE of 21.0% and a robust ROCE of 27.7%, both significantly outperforming sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E12, E13]. Financial health is pristine as the company is almost debt-free with borrowings dropping to Rs 4 Cr and a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x [E37, E39, E59]. Operating momentum is exceptionally strong, driven by a 62% surge in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and quarterly operating margins expanding by 9 percentage points year-over-year [E21, E31]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 5,429 per share against the current market price of Rs 1,610, offering a massive 70.3% margin of safety [E45, E46]. Conceded: [E16].

The structural revenue engine of the business shows clear signs of deceleration, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of just 1% over the last 3 years and a modest 5% over 10 years [E16, E14]. This top-line sluggishness is further underscored by historical data showing poor sales growth of 8.22% over the past five years [E60]. Compounding these growth concerns, the company operates in a cyclical earnings profile that is seasonally weak in March, June, and September, while its yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are both explicitly categorized as inconsistent [E32, E33, E57]. Furthermore, price momentum has detached from operational fundamentals, with recent price growth exceeding profit growth by 21% and 5-year price growth outpacing profit growth, signaling that expectations are running ahead of actual delivery [E55, E56]. Conceded: the company boasts an impressive TTM operating margin of 27% and strong cash conversion backed by Rs 72 Cr in free cash flow [E30, E36]. Yet, technical and volatility risks loom large as the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a severe annualised volatility of 68.7% [E50, E53]. Finally, management explicitly warns that global trade uncertainties, regional conflicts, and potential tariff measures by major economies like the United States warrant continued caution [E76, E77].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over 3 years is a modest 1% [E16] and the 5-year sales growth is 8.22% [E60]. However, this historical sluggishness completely overlooks the dramatic acceleration happening right now, where trailing twelve-month sales growth has surged to 15% [E17] and rules-based screening flags recent quarterly spikes with sales up 22% year-over-year [E62]. The bear's concern over inconsistent margin trends [E32, E33] is heavily outweighed by actual margin expansion, as TTM operating margin reached 27% (up 4 percentage points) and quarterly margin hit 28% in September 2026 (up 9 percentage points) [E30, E31]. While the bear highlights price-to-fundamental divergence [E55, E56], this is entirely justified by a massive 62% surge in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21] and a top-tier rules-based screen score of 91 out of 100 indicating high conviction [E61]. Conceded: the stock trades below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50] and management flags global trade caution [E76, E77], but these technical headwinds and macro worries are neutralized by pristine fundamentals including a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x [E37], robust free cash flow of Rs 72 Cr [E36], and a supportive chemical sector tailwind score of +0.55 [E68].

Conceded: TTM sales growth reached 15% and recent quarterly sales rose 22% [E17, E62]. However, dismissing a multi-year trend of sluggish top-line performance ignores the reality of 1% 3-year compounded sales growth and a 5-year rate of just 8.22% [E16, E60]. The bull points to margin expansion, yet official records explicitly label the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends as inconsistent [E32, E33]. While the bull excuses price-led expectations using recent profit acceleration [E21], the signals note that expectations are running ahead of delivery with price growth exceeding profit growth [E56]. Furthermore, the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50], and management itself warns that geopolitical volatility, regional conflicts, and US tariff measures warrant continued caution [E76, E77].

Conceded: the 3-year compounded sales growth is 1% [E16] and the 5-year rate is 8.22% [E60]. However, this multi-year lagging figure is superseded by a powerful acceleration where TTM sales growth hit 15% and recent quarterly sales surged 22% [E17, E62], proving the top line has decisively broken out of its historical range. While the bear cites inconsistent margin trends [E32, E33], operating margins have actually climbed to 27% in TTM against 23% three years prior, and reached 28% in the latest September quarter [E30, E31]. Conceded: price growth has recently outpaced profit growth [E56] and the stock sits below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50]. Nevertheless, these technical indicators completely ignore the massive fundamental value anchored by a pristine balance sheet with borrowings slashed to just ₹ 4 Cr [E39], a stellar ROE of 21.0% [E13], and a staggering 70.3% margin of safety backed by an intrinsic DCF value of ₹ 5,429 per share [E45, E46].

Conceded: TTM sales growth reached 15% and recent quarterly sales surged 22% [E17, E62]. However, the bull's dismissal of the multi-year top-line stagnation glosses over a severe structural weakness, namely the anaemic 3-year compounded sales growth of 1% and the poor 5-year rate of 8.22% [E16, E60]. Furthermore, while the bull highlights rising operating margins [E30, E31], it ignores the explicit official filing classification that the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are "Inconsistent" over the last three years and two quarters respectively [E32, E33]. The bull's defense of technical weakness as irrelevant to fundamental value [E50] ignores the reality of high annualised volatility sitting at 68.7% alongside price growth outpacing profit growth by 21%, which proves that market expectations are running well ahead of actual delivery [E53, E56]. Finally, the reliance on a pristine balance sheet and DCF projections [E39, E45] completely overlooks external trade and tariff uncertainties explicitly flagged by management as risks to international supply chains following United States trade measures [E76, E77].
